summary: Added write_chart_edits<W: Write + ?Sized> with complete pre-write validation, shared edit planning and borrowed output chunks. Added WritePatchError with typed sources and eight integration tests. All required checks passed.

commands.outcome: Passed twice, including after the final implementation correction.
Passed twice: 165 existing unit tests and 8 new integration tests; 0 failed, 0 ignored; 0 doctests.
Passed twice with warnings denied, including after the final correction.
Passed twice, including the final implementation.

design_decisions: Both public edit paths use plan_chart_edits, the existing Planner, the same sorted span validation, and the same splice_chunks iterator. All bounds and overlaps are checked before the writer is called, preserving the existing error ordering and insertion ordering.

The writer and unchanged XML are borrowed. Replacement and series-clone fragments remain planner-owned. The streaming path passes borrowed slices directly to write_all and never collects or clones the full document to feed the writer.

WritePatchError owns either the original PatchError or the original io::Error. Error::source returns that exact typed cause. I/O payload allocation identity is tested. PatchError gains only the additive Error implementation.

write_all provides short-write, Interrupted, and WriteZero behavior. Other I/O errors stop emission immediately and may leave a prefix. Documentation distinguishes validation atomicity from the absence of I/O rollback. The API never flushes or takes ownership of the writer.

Existing signatures, variants, public struct fields, and exhaustive matching remain unchanged. The new error models the two fixed failure domains. User-specified slice parameters and compatibility requirements take precedence over unrelated API generalization or non_exhaustive migrations.

Cloning a series now checks an empty template list, template bounds, and index/order span bounds rather than allowing malformed public coordinates to panic. The original template/fragment length consistency checks are preserved as recoverable errors.

Integration tests exercise every edit operation against the buffered API, equal-offset insertion order, combined structural/value edits, byte preservation, trait-object writers, writer reuse, late invalid/overlapping spans, planner failures, short writes, Interrupted, WriteZero, custom I/O payload identity, and direct borrowing for no-edit output.
limitations: This was an isolated component implementation using the supplied pinned crate and cached dependencies; no full document-engine, UI, or visual validation was performed.
No allocator benchmark or peak-memory metric was measured. Streaming allocation behavior is supported by code structure and the no-edit input-pointer test, not a quantitative performance claim.
ChartData must describe the same XML as documented by the existing API; this change does not authenticate scan provenance or add semantic chart validation.
